post.description:
Starts a WebAuthn registration ceremony for the currently
authenticated user. The challenge is keyed against the
user's session so it cannot be replayed against a
different account.

The server returns ceremony options
(`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions`) that the browser
uses to invoke the platform authenticator.

Returns 503 if passkey support is not configured.
post.summary: Begin linking a passkey to the authenticated account

401.description: Unauthorized - User is not authenticated via session

503.description: Service Unavailable - Passkey support not configured

post.description:
Completes a WebAuthn registration ceremony started by
`/auth/link/passkey/begin`, attaching the verified passkey
to the currently authenticated user via
`AuthService.RegisterPasskey`.

The browser posts the attestation response
(`credential_id`, `client_data_json`, `authenticator_data`,
`signature`) and the `session_key` from the matching /begin.
The server verifies the challenge, origin, RP ID, and
attestation signature, then persists the credential via
`AuthService.RegisterPasskey` with the authenticated user
as both `user_id` and `requester_id`.
post.summary: Finish linking a passkey to the authenticated account

400.description: Bad Request - Invalid request body or malformed attestation

401.description: Unauthorized - User is not authenticated, or challenge mismatch

503.description: Service Unavailable - Passkey support not configured

post.description:
Starts a WebAuthn assertion (login) ceremony.

The server generates a random challenge and returns the
ceremony options (`PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions`) for
the browser. The challenge is stored server-side and must
be presented to the matching `/finish` endpoint for
verification. The flow is discoverable (no user identity
required up front) -- the browser's authenticator selects
which passkey to use and the User Handle is supplied with
the assertion.

Returns 503 if passkey support is not configured.

503.description: Service Unavailable - Passkey support not configured

post.description:
Completes a WebAuthn assertion (login) ceremony started by
`/auth/passkey/login/begin`.

The browser posts the assertion (`credential_id`,
`client_data_json`, `authenticator_data`, `signature`) and
the `session_key` from the matching /begin. The server
resolves the user from the User Handle, verifies the
signature against the stored public key, bumps the sign
counter via `AuthService.UpdatePasskeyCounter`, and logs
the user in.

400.description: Bad Request - Invalid request body or expired ceremony

401.description: Unauthorized - Challenge mismatch, invalid signature, or unknown credential

503.description: Service Unavailable - Passkey support not configured

post.description:
Starts a WebAuthn registration ceremony for a new passkey.

The server generates a random challenge and returns the
ceremony options (`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions`) that
the browser uses to invoke the platform authenticator. The
challenge is stored server-side and must be presented to
the matching `/finish` endpoint for verification.

Returns 503 if passkey support is not configured
(`WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` unset).

503.description: Service Unavailable - Passkey support not configured

post.description:
Completes a WebAuthn registration ceremony started by
`/auth/passkey/register/begin`.

The browser posts the attestation response
(`credential_id`, `client_data_json`, `authenticator_data`,
`signature`) and the `session_key` from the matching /begin.
The server verifies the challenge, origin, RP ID, and
attestation signature, then persists the credential via
`AuthService.RegisterPasskey`. The User Handle supplied at
/begin must already exist (see PostPasskeyRegisterBegin).

400.description: Bad Request - Invalid request body or expired ceremony

401.description: Unauthorized - Challenge mismatch or invalid attestation

503.description: Service Unavailable - Passkey support not configured

Streams the activity log for everything the requesting user is
allowed to view. Use `mode=most_used` to stream aggregated note
scores instead; the `algorithm` query parameter then selects the
scoring function (count or log_count).

For entries that reference a note (`note_id` is non-empty), the
response embeds `note_title` and `note_content` into the JSON
document carried in `metadata_json`, so a single request can be
used to render history without further per-note lookups.

Reports DNS reachability and service-level reachability for
Garage (S3), SpiceDB (gRPC), imgproxy (HTTP /health), the
WerSu gRPC backend, and Postgres (when DATABASE_DSN is set).
The response is always returned with HTTP 200; inspect the
`overall_ok` and per-service `reachable` flags for health.

address.description:
Address that was probed (host:port) for the service-level checks, or
the host portion for DNS-level checks.

detail.description:
Detail is an optional human-readable note for the response (e.g.
the gRPC status name, the number of buckets returned, ...).

latency_ms.description:
LatencyMs measures how long the probe took. Zero if the probe was
skipped (e.g. DNS already failed).

shelf_id.description:
Either ShelfId or DirectoryIds must be provided; the gRPC server
resolves rules against the shelf and auto-selects a directory when
only ShelfId is set.

error.description:
Error is a convenience field that mirrors the first non-empty error
from DNS or Service, so monitoring can read the top-level state
without traversing the nested checks.

avatar_url.description:
AvatarURL is the absolute URL to the user's avatar. Empty
string (the protobuf zero-value) renders as JSON null, so
the frontend sees `avatar_url: null` when no provider has
resolved an avatar.
